text:
maria: quick sync after the cutover RFC. proposing a small lease/orchestration surface so proxies can deterministically acquire write authority during migrations. want to call out tradeoffs before we commit.
aj: what endpoints are you imagining?
maria: minimal API: POST /lease/claim, POST /lease/renew, POST /lease/release, GET /lease/info. default TTL 20s, but callers can request up to 120s for long ops.
jonathan: claim scope: per-tenant+shard vs per-shard-zone?
maria: prefer per-shard-zone (tenant set + shard id + region zone) so we can do coarse batching without exploding object counts. we still encode tenant set in the token so enforcement is possible.
kate: if control plane is partitioned, do proxies block or serve? that's the core availability vs correctness tradeoff.
maria: proxies should have a fast local policy: try to claim with a 150ms deadline; on timeout fall back to one of three actions (configurable per-tenant): (1) proxy-forward-to-active, (2) serve-readonly, (3) serve-local-with-audit. Default hosted customers get option (2).
devin: how do we prevent two proxies from both thinking they have the lease during races?
maria: server uses a CAS on a linearizable store; response contains a monotonic epoch and signature: `lease_sig`. proxies must present `X-Lease-Sig` on write ops.
aj: signature format? JWT or HMAC?
maria: prefer short-lived signed JWT-ish blob: {lease_id, epoch, allowed_shards, exp, provider_id} signed by control-plane key. lightweight and verifiable offline. bind to proxy-id and TLS client cert when possible.
jonathan: are reads allowed without lease? sometimes reads are okay under consent flags. need to codify read vs write authority.
maria: define `write_authority` == lease. reads allowed when `consent_policy` for tenant permits cross-region reads; proxies check `X-Region-Consent: <policy-id>` header.
kate: telemetry and operator signals?
devin: expose metrics: lease_claim_latency_ms, lease_claim_fail_rate, lease_staleness_count, lease_bundle_refreshes. also emit structured audit events: claim, renew, revoke with actor, reason, and correlation_id.
maria: add a revocation endpoint POST /lease/revoke for emergency kills. can be RBAC gated.
aj: rollout and safety: if we give proxies bundle tokens (signed bundles covering N shards) we reduce control-plane load, but increase blast radius if tokens leaked.
maria: mitigation: short expiry (default 45s), binding to proxy instance id, and a revocation blacklist that proxies check occasionally.
jonathan: operator UX for cutovers: suggest an automated graceful-handback window. when new region gets leases, keep old region leases valid in grace mode for 90s with write-fallback telemetry. route 5-10% traffic back to old region until metrics converge.
kate: include runbook snippets: commands like `leasectl revoke --tenant t-42 --shard s3` and `leasectl list --region eu-west --active`. also an alert playbook for excessive lease-churn.
maria: implementation detail: backing store should be strongly consistent (etcd/consensus) for correctness. we can front with a cache for reads but writes must go to leader.
ops-bot: deployment note: `lease-orchestrator v0.1.0` promoted to staging at 1725004600
aj: in staging we saw transient 409 conflict on concurrent claims. client should do jittered backoff max 4 tries. log conflict with sample rate 1%.
devin: add prometheus counters and a kinesis audit stream for replay. retention 90 days. also emit `lease_bundle_issued` events.
maria: security: rotate signing keys monthly, support KMS-backed signing, and require mTLS for proxy requests.
aj: config toggle per-tenant: `control_plane_fail_policy` = [deny, allow_read_only, allow_full]. default deny for hosted, allow_read_only for enterprise opting in.
kate: I'll draft runbook + dashboard wireframe: show active leases, recent revocations, per-tenant policy, and a "cutover health" score combining lease success %, p99 acquire latency, and write error rate.
jonathan: timeline: prototype in 2 weeks, internal-only canary, then proxy opt-in, then tenant opt-in toggles.
maria: final owners: aj (token format + signing), devin (metrics + audit + revocation), kate (runbook + dashboard), jonathan (operator rollback). I'll assemble follow-up RFC with APIs. :thumbsup:
